about: Whether a DDC monitor reports its brightness, and what the slider shows after a write (ReadState on both apps). A write-only monitor never answers a read; the slider is its only record of the level.

cases.name: a user write taken by an unreadable monitor makes it write-only
a user write refused by an unreadable monitor makes it silent
a refused write leaves a write-only monitor write-only
a readable monitor stays readable after a refused write
a reading is the current level
a write-only monitor's current level is its slider
an unknown monitor without a reading is left alone
a silent monitor cannot be used
a write-only monitor can be used
a taken write is the level the monitor last took
a refused write keeps the level it last took
a refused write with nothing taken yet knows no level
a write-only monitor's slider goes back after a refused write
a taken write leaves the slider where it is
a readable monitor's next reading corrects the slider instead
a monitor that never took a write becomes silent, the slider stays
a write-only monitor with no level taken yet leaves the slider
